description:
One query vs N candidates (1k / 234k words). Baseline: our Elixir Levenshtein (optimise further). NIF column: ex_strsim 0.1.0 (exact Levenshtein, per pair, normal scheduler) called via Enum.map over candidates, as a real user would batch. fuzler is not Levenshtein (normalisation, token overlap, rounding): header note only, not installed (its rustler_precompiled pin conflicts with ex_strsim). Separate script from the fuzzy_search app, which stays a supporting showcase. Agreement: identical distances.

Evidence bar (from defk-dtw.4/defk-dtw.15): script examples/<name>.exs with Mix.install of the pinned anchor package; the anchor's Elixir version is the first baseline and must be optimised further in Elixir before the verdict counts (what was tried listed in the header; baseline: :optimized); realistic size declared in the header before any numbers; workload verdict at the realistic size, other size beside; ~6-point geometric sweep with crossover (smallest size where defk >= 2x, or none), skipped if a large run exceeds ~1 min; NIF timing and responsiveness (max and p99 1 ms tick gap, one scheduler, large size, for Elixir/defk/NIF) via Defk.Bench.report/1; Elixir, defk and NIF outputs must agree (failure fails the script); quiet-machine run_all.exs; row added to examples/README.md.

comments.text: Done on branch defk-9p6.11/batched-levenshtein (commit f7cd20e): examples/batched_levenshtein.exs, Mix.install ex_strsim 0.1.0 (precompiled, installed fine). PROVISIONAL, MEASURED UNDER LOAD (two other benchmark agents running). Realistic size declared: 234,454 words (fuzzy_search list), query 'accomodation'; 1k is the sweep's first point. Elixir variants at 234k (best of 5): anchor per_pair DP 179 ms; DP with fixed query row 157 (binary) / 158 (charlist); Myers binary 28.1; Myers charlist 18.9; Myers binary comprehension 56.9; + branch-free score 16.3; over persistent_term tuple 16.0; same in 12 chunks 3.6-4.2 ms (baseline from 10k words up; one process below). defk (same Myers, [u8] out, packed index in persistent_term): DP kernel 31.3; Myers one call 6.6-6.8 (5.7 without the list); 12 chunks 4.3-4.6. Verdict at 234k: 0.86-0.99x -> poor (best vs best, geo_nearest's rule); one process 2.4-2.8x; sweep 1k 2.9-4x, 3k 2.7-3.4x, 10k 1.9-2.3x, 30k ~1x, 100k 0.83-1.17x, 234k 0.84-1.0x; crossover 1000. defk chunks run on 2 of 12 schedulers (defk-8qs; yield or 1 ms sleep before the call did not help). ex_strsim per pair via Enum.map 35-38 ms (defk 8x, Elixir one-process Myers 2.2x faster). Tick gap (one scheduler, 234k, one process each): max ~2.0 / 2.2 / 2.1 ms Elixir/defk/ex_strsim, the loaded machine's floor (short per-pair NIF calls do not block). Agreement: Elixir (Myers, DP, chunked), defk (Myers, DP, chunked), anchor and ex_strsim identical on 11 queries x 234k, query lengths 0..70 x 1k, odd candidates (empty, 64-300 bytes); kernels agree with Elixir mode; mismatch exits 1. Expected :poor; a 1.0x run could read marginal (defk-9p6.24). README row in the poor-fit section. mix test and mix ci pass. No compiler bug found; Myers needed no workaround (i64, m <= 62).

title: Target workload: batched Levenshtein vs ex_strsim
